plan: Map (findings 2, 3, 5, 6, 7): in `src/mapLayout.ts`, `denied:<host>` nodes get `active` when a blocked event for that host is less than ACTIVE_MS old. In `src/ShieldMap.tsx`, a `MapControls` child in a `Panel` uses `useReactFlow()` (zoomIn/zoomOut/fitView) with a motiv `IconButtonGroup`, and `<Controls>` is removed. The `setNodes` effect merges by id: it keeps the current node object (with `measured` and `dragging`) and makes a new object only when `position` or the compared data fields (label, tone, badges, active, title) changed. `onNodeDragStop` saves `{...layout, ...dragged}` and never prunes. Pruning happens in a separate effect only after the inputs have loaded: `ShieldPage` passes `folders` as `undefined` until `listFolders` returns for this shield, and `folder:*` ids are skipped while it is undefined. ShieldMap registers its own `getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent` listener. It uses `screenToFlowPosition` and the boundary node's position plus `measured` size to test the drop point against the full boundary rect, then calls a new `onDropFolder(path)` prop. The listener in `App.tsx` then handles only `data-drop="rail"`. Symlink (finding 4): a new Rust command `resolve_folder(path) -> String` wraps `shield::host_dir` (`commands.rs`, `lib.rs`, `api.ts`). Both drop paths call it first. The mount confirm in `SettingsTab.tsx` and the rail confirm card in `ShieldRail.tsx` show the canonical path, plus "link to <target>" when it differs from the dropped path. The guest path comes from the canonical basename, and `addMount`/`createShield` get the canonical path. App terminal (finding 8): `Manager::attach_app` returns a `u64` token stored next to the sink in `AppOutput`. A new `detach_app(session_id, token)` clears the sink only when the token matches. `TerminalPane.tsx` ignores output after `disposed`, detaches in cleanup, and detaches at once if it is disposed while `await attachApp` runs. Draft (finding 9): `ShieldPage.tsx` keeps the ElasticTabs block mounted with `hidden` when the view is chat/terminal/app, and keeps the last tab value in state, so the SettingsTab mount draft and the Finder-drop confirm survive tree navigation. Row actions (finding 1): `ShieldRail.tsx` gets one motiv `IconButton` (lucide `Ellipsis`) per item. It opens a small menu made of a motiv `Card` and ghost `Button`s, and right-click and Shift+F10/ContextMenu on the focused treeitem open the same menu. Apps get Edit (intent `app` with `appId`, which `AppsSection` opens as an edit draft), Restart (`restartApp`) and Delete (`removeApp`, with confirm). Terminals get Close. Chats get Rename (inline motiv field) and Delete (with confirm). Chat rename is stored host-side as `chat_titles: BTreeMap<String,String>` on the shield config. `list_chats` applies it, and `list()` excludes it from the pendingRestart compare, as it does for layout. I recommend this over pi `set_session_name` because pi can rename only its current session: a rename would switch the user's open chat, it needs a running VM, and `read_chat` misses a `session_info` line written after `CHAT_HEAD` in long chats. Chat delete is a new `agent::delete_chat(state, id)`. It accepts only ids that `list_chats` accepts, opens `sessions` with NOFOLLOW|DIRECTORY, checks with `statat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` that the entry is a regular file, and calls `unlinkat`. If the deleted chat is pi's current chat, the UI first sends `new_session`. App.tsx records each shield's current chat from AgentsTab `onChat`. Rust tests cover delete_chat (it refuses links, dirs, bad names and a linked sessions dir), the chat title overlay and its removal on delete, and attach/detach token semantics (a stale detach keeps the new sink).
risks: Host-side chat titles differ from the task text ('pi set_session_name'). The other model or the reviewer can reject this deviation. Pi's own session list does not show the zwinger title.

Keeping the tab panels mounted while hidden keeps ShieldMap and NetworkTab rendering in a display:none container. React Flow can measure 0 size, and fitView can be wrong when the map is mounted hidden first. Call fitView again when the map becomes visible.
Two window-wide onDragDropEvent listeners (map and rail) must not both act on one drop. Each must check that the drop point is inside its own element.
The node merge must compare data that contains a component reference (`icon`) and arrays (`badges`). A shallow compare that misses a field leaves stale labels or tones on screen.
Deleting the chat that a running pi has open: if `new_session` fails or arrives late, pi can append to a deleted (unlinked) file, and that chat comes back as orphaned output.

The popover menu built from motiv Card/Button needs focus management (focus the first item, Escape to close, close on outside click). It must not conflict with the tree's keyboard handler or with the dnd-kit Space key.
claim_reason: All nine findings are fixes inside the code that round 01 wrote with opus as implementer (ShieldMap merge, attach_app sink, rail tree, drop listener). Continuity lowers the risk of regressions in the tree keyboard and dnd-kit wiring.
backlog: Show a zwinger chat title in pi too: sync it with set_session_name the next time that chat is current
Lift all per-shield drafts (mount, app, secret) into one App-level draft store, so that they also survive a shield switch
Undo for chat and app delete (soft delete with a short undo toast)
Proper accessible context-menu component in @driif/motiv (Menu/Popover), to replace the local Card-based menu
